title: Example feature for a Next.js + Postgres app
summary: A small but complete draft card used by the validator tests. Every rule should pass on this file.

checklist.text: Validate every request body on the server before using it.
Add an index for every column used in a frequent lookup.
Log failed requests without logging request bodies.

decisions.question: How many requests per second do you expect at launch?

options.name: Built-in framework feature
best_fit_when: You want the fewest moving parts
avoid_when: You need features the framework does not offer

options.name: Managed service
avoid_when: Per-request pricing hurts at your scale

notes: Route Handlers receive `params` as a Promise: await it.

verify.check: A request with an invalid body returns HTTP 400 and changes nothing.
The main lookup query uses an index scan, not a sequential scan.
Log lines for failed requests never contain the request body.

body.why: The built-in feature keeps the code close to the data and adds no new service. Choose the managed service when you need it working today and the price is acceptable.

lenses.security:
Validate input on the server and keep request bodies out of logs.

```ts
const body = schema.parse(await request.json());
```
lenses.performance: Index the columns you look up most often and check the query plan.

body.mistakes:
- Trusting client-side validation.
- Logging full request bodies.
- Adding the feature without an index.
